title: Amazon Fire TV — Install and Set Up BM TV Enabler
excerpt: Install the Android phone enabler, choose the correct Fire TV and enable BM Remote Control.
pages: Prepare and install the phone app
Check what you need

An Android phone, your Fire TV/Firestick, their home Wi-Fi and BM Remote Helper already installed and open on the TV. BM TV Enabler is for an Android phone, not iPhone or the TV. It enables BM Remote Control; it cannot switch on the TV’s ADB debugging setting remotely.
Switch on TV debugging

On the TV: Settings > My Fire TV > Developer options > ADB debugging > ON. If Developer options is missing: My Fire TV > About, highlight the device name and press Select seven times, then go Back. Leave the TV awake. Do not expose debugging to the internet or forward its port on your router.
Get the official Enabler download

In BM Support Install Guides, choose TV Remote Enabler and press Get the app link. Scan the QR with your Android phone’s camera, or tap Already on your phone? Tap here to download. Download the APK on the phone, not on the Fire TV.
Install on your Android phone

Open the downloaded APK from your browser’s Downloads or the phone’s Files app. If blocked, choose Settings and allow installs from that browser/Files app, then return and press Install. Open BM TV Enabler. If Android refuses the file or shows a warning you do not understand, ask BM Support rather than disabling phone security features.
Select and enable the right Fire TV
Join the same home Wi-Fi

Connect the Android phone to the same home network as the Fire TV; do not use mobile data or an isolated guest network. Different Wi-Fi bands are fine if your router allows devices to communicate. Keep BM Remote Helper open on the TV and note the TV’s address.
Find your TV

In BM TV Enabler, press Find my TV. It lists discoverable Amazon Fire TVs by name and address. Choose the one matching the address shown by BM Remote Helper, then press Use this TV. If several devices have similar names, the address is the deciding check. Searching does not enable any TV automatically.
Deal with an unreachable-debugging label

A listed TV with unreachable debugging may have ADB debugging off, be asleep or be blocked by Wi-Fi isolation. Check the TV’s debugging switch and wake it. The label is not proof that debugging is off. If no TV appears, type the address shown in the helper; not every Fire TV advertises itself.
Start enabling and approve on the TV

Press Turn on remote control on the phone and keep the app open. Watch the TV for Allow USB debugging? / Allow debugging? Tick Always allow from this computer if offered, then choose Allow. This approval authorises the Enabler’s connection from your phone; it is separate from screen-sharing consent.
Confirm setup and solve problems
Wait for the success message

Wait while the Enabler checks the TV, installs BM Remote Control if needed and enables its service. Continue only when the phone says Remote control is on. You can close this app. If an error appears, read it and complete the missing step before pressing Try again.
Return to remote help

Leave BM Remote Helper installed on the TV. Use the separate Amazon Fire TV — Use Remote Help guide to connect through a staff invitation in your own ticket or secure order. Enabling the control service alone does not start a screen share.
If connection or permission fails

Check the helper’s address again, same Wi-Fi, TV awake and ADB debugging ON. If you refused the debugging prompt, retry and approve the new prompt. If a previously saved permission does not work, ask staff to guide you through the TV’s debugging authorisations; do not factory-reset the TV. Router isolation can also prevent connection.
Understand what stays saved

Debugging and the enabled control service normally stay saved across ordinary TV restarts. You do not normally repeat this setup every time the TV powers on. The router may change the TV’s address; check it before retrying. A factory reset, app removal or some system updates may require setup again. If you turn debugging off after support, turn it on again before any future Enabler setup.
safety: Only share with BM Support staff through your own support ticket or secure order. Do not post your TV code publicly. Anything visible on the TV may be seen by staff: close banking, payment, password and other private screens first. You can decline a request or end a session.

title: Amazon Fire TV — Install BM Remote Helper
excerpt: Download and install the official TV helper, prepare Fire TV permissions and complete remote-control setup.
pages: Download the TV app
Prepare your devices

Have the Fire TV/Firestick awake, its normal remote, internet access, and a phone or computer signed in to BM Support. Use the Amazon/Fire TV download and guide, not the Android/Google TV instructions. Installation and screen-share consent are separate.
Get the official current app

Sign in at bmsupport.uk, open Install Guides, then Download BM Support Apps. Find the current remote app (listed as BM Support Remote). Press Request download link, then View download options. Use the current official link; if it has expired, request a fresh one. Do not use APKs from unrelated websites.
Download on the Fire TV

On the TV, open Downloader. If it is not installed, get Downloader from the TV’s app store first, open it and accept its initial prompts. On your phone, display the official download options, then type the complete download URL into Downloader on the TV and select Go. Wait for the download to finish. Do not enter the TV’s six-digit pairing code here: this field needs the download URL.
Allow installation and open the app

If installation is blocked, open Settings > My Fire TV > Developer options > Install unknown apps and switch on Downloader (or the app named in the prompt). Older Fire OS versions use Apps from Unknown Sources. If Developer options is hidden: Settings > My Fire TV > About, highlight the device name and press Select seven times, then go Back. Return to Downloader and choose Install. Select Open when installation finishes.
Prepare the Helper and remote control
Check the app you opened

The remote package is currently listed as BM Support Remote in the download list; the TV help screen is BM Remote Helper. If the downloaded build instead opens the BM Support app and offers Install Remote Helper, use that in-app installer and approve Install. Do not use the removed standalone customer-helper page.
Complete helper installation prompts

Follow the helper’s installation/setup prompts for BM Remote Control if offered. If asked to allow this app to install another app, enable the specifically named source, return and approve the installation. Do not repeatedly re-download the APK while an active share is running.
Prepare Amazon’s external Enabler

Newer Fire OS blocks the TV from enabling its own remote control. Use the separate Amazon Fire TV — Install and Set Up BM TV Enabler guide on an Android phone on the same Wi-Fi. Turn ADB debugging ON on the TV and follow the phone’s instructions; ADB debugging alone does not mean remote control is ready.
Check successful setup

Finish only when the phone Enabler confirms Remote control is on. Reopen BM Remote Helper on the TV and verify it displays the TV’s address and a six-digit pairing code. Note the address for setup and the code for a help session: they serve different purposes.
Ready checks and installation troubleshooting
Keep the correct apps

Keep BM Remote Helper and BM Remote Control installed. BM TV Enabler stays on the Android phone. Do not install the Enabler on the TV or expect it to replace the Helper. Once installation is complete, optional unknown-source permissions can be turned off until the next update.
If installation is blocked

Recheck Install unknown apps for the source actually doing the install. If Install/Open is off-screen, scroll the installer. If an existing install causes a signature/version conflict, stop sharing and contact BM Support before uninstalling, because uninstalling clears setup.
If remote control is not ready

Complete the separate Enabler guide, including the TV debugging approval. If the TV’s address is missing, check its network connection and reopen the helper. If it remains missing, ask staff; do not guess an address. Android/Google TV Accessibility instructions are not the Amazon workaround.
Move on to everyday use

Use Amazon Fire TV — Use Remote Help for staff invitation, six-digit code entry, TV approval, screen sharing, chat and ending a session. A successful install does not grant staff permanent access. Only share with BM Support staff through your own support ticket or secure order. Do not post your TV code publicly. Anything visible on the TV may be seen by staff: close banking, payment, password and other private screens first. You can decline a request or end a session.

title: Amazon Fire TV — Use Remote Help
excerpt: Connect your Fire TV to a staff-requested ticket or order screen share, chat and end the session safely.
pages: Prepare and enter the TV code
Prepare the correct TV

Switch on the TV and open BM Remote Helper. Leave it open so the current six-digit code is visible. If remote control is needed, complete the installation/setup guide first. For Amazon, complete the Enabler setup as well.
Open your existing help conversation

On your phone or computer, sign in to BM Support. For a ticket, open Tickets and select your own ticket. For a sale, open your own order and its secure checkout; enter that order’s password if asked. Return to the original conversation, not the staff TV Remote page.
Wait for staff to invite you

Ask the staff member in that conversation to request a screen share. The request must belong to this ticket or order. An invitation/code-entry action appears in the conversation. If it is missing, ask staff to send the request; do not use a standalone TV-helper page.
Enter the TV code

Open the screen-share invitation. In the pop-up, enter all six digits exactly as shown in BM Remote Helper, including any leading zero, then press Connect TV. Use the code from the TV you actually want help with. If the code is rejected, reopen the helper to check the current code and try again.
Approve sharing and work with staff
Wait for the staff member to answer

Keep BM Remote Helper open on the TV while staff answers the request. Code entry links the TV to this help request; it does not replace the TV’s permission prompts. Do not start another request while this one is connecting.
Approve the connection on the TV

When BM Remote Helper asks to allow the staff connection, check the request and choose Allow. If the TV asks to start recording or casting, choose Start now or Start. Android wording varies. Decline if you did not request help. Staff cannot see your screen until the required sharing approval is given.
Check the Screen share tab

Once connected, your ticket/order switches to Screen share. Ask staff in the same conversation to confirm that they can see your TV picture. Keep the TV awake and the helper running. The ticket’s original conversation remains available; its chat pop-out can be used while the share is open.
Let staff help you

If remote control was enabled during setup, staff can operate the TV during the session. Without that permission, staff may only see the screen and talk you through actions. Follow their guidance using your normal remote when needed. Tell them before opening private information.
End safely and reconnect
Finish the session

Use End session on the customer Screen share view when help is finished; staff can also end the session. Check that the sharing/connected indicator clears. If the page is unavailable or the indicator does not clear, stop sharing in BM Remote Helper on the TV or close the helper to stop the picture.
Start a later session

A new session needs a new staff invitation through your ticket/order and the current TV code, followed by the TV’s permission prompts. An old code or invitation must not be treated as permission for ongoing access.
If there is no picture

Keep the helper open and the TV awake; confirm you approved both Allow and the recording/casting prompt. Ask staff whether they have joined this exact ticket/order. If the picture remains black, end the session on both sides, reopen the helper, and repeat with a fresh invitation/code. Do not reinstall or reset the TV before speaking to staff.
If control or code entry fails

No code box: ask staff to send/re-send the screen-share invitation in this conversation. Rejected code: verify all six digits and the correct TV. Picture but no control: check the setup guide’s remote-control permission steps. Lost internet: reconnect and ask staff for a new session. Ordinary TV restarts do not normally require reinstalling the apps.
safety: Only share with BM Support staff through your own support ticket or secure order. Do not post your TV code publicly. Anything visible on the TV may be seen by staff: close banking, payment, password and other private screens first. You can decline a request or end a session.

title: Android / Google TV — Install and Set Up BM Remote Helper
excerpt: Install the TV helper and grant the Accessibility permissions required for remote control.
pages: Download and install
Prepare the correct TV

Have your Android TV/Google TV box or television awake, its remote and internet access. Keep a phone or computer signed in to BM Support for the download link. Follow the Android/Google TV instructions; BM TV Enabler and the Fire TV debugging workaround are not needed for this platform.
Get the official current app

Sign in at bmsupport.uk, open Install Guides, then Download BM Support Apps. Find the current remote app (listed as BM Support Remote). Press Request download link, then View download options. Use the current official link; if it has expired, request a fresh one. Do not use APKs from unrelated websites.
Download onto the TV

On the TV, open Downloader. If it is not installed, get Downloader from the TV’s app store first, open it and accept its initial prompts. On your phone, display the official download options, then type the complete download URL into Downloader on the TV and select Go. Wait for the download to finish. Do not enter the TV’s six-digit pairing code here: this field needs the download URL.
Allow the installer

If installation is blocked, open the settings prompt and allow this source. Depending on the TV, this is Settings > Apps > Special app access > Install unknown apps, or Settings > Security & restrictions > Unknown sources. Enable only Downloader or the installer named in the prompt, return to the downloaded file and choose Install, then Open. Menu names vary by brand and Android version.
Install the control app and grant Accessibility
Open and complete Helper setup

Open BM Remote Helper (the download may be labelled BM Support Remote). Follow its setup prompts for BM Remote Control. If a separate control-app installation is offered, approve Install. If asked to allow installs from the Helper/BM Support app, enable that named source, go Back and retry its installer. Keep both Helper and Control installed.
Open Accessibility settings

From the remote-control setup prompt, open Accessibility. Alternatively use TV Settings > Accessibility, or Settings > Device Preferences/System > Accessibility, depending on the TV. Look under Downloaded apps or Services for BM Remote Control. Select it. Choose Use service/Enable and confirm the system warning with Allow/OK.
If Android blocks the service

Some sideloaded installs show Restricted setting or For your security, this setting is currently unavailable. Open Settings > Apps > See all apps > BM Remote Control, then its three-dot menu if available, and choose Allow restricted settings. Confirm using the device’s normal security prompt, then return to Accessibility and enable the service. Apply this to the app whose service is blocked, not an unrelated app.
If the restricted-settings option is missing

Do not force the switch, disable security protection or assume debugging solves it. Ask BM Support to check the current official build and supported in-app/session installer for your device. Menu locations and sideload restrictions vary. The control app’s Accessibility service must actually be enabled for remote operation; having the Helper installed alone is not enough.
Check setup and get ready to connect
Verify remote-control permission

Return to the Helper and check its remote-control status. If it remains off, reopen Accessibility and verify BM Remote Control is enabled, then return. If the switch turns itself off, stop and ask staff to check device compatibility or the installation method. Screen viewing may still work without remote-control permission.
Keep sharing consent separate

Accessibility permission enables remote operation; it does not approve the screen recording/casting prompt for a particular session. When staff connects later, you must also approve Allow and Start now/Start on the TV when asked. Do not grant access to a request you did not make.
Finish the installation checks

Confirm the Helper shows a six-digit code and keep it installed. Ordinary restarts normally retain Accessibility settings; some TV software may reset permissions, so check them if control stops. Turn off optional unknown-source permission after installation if desired; you may need it again for updates.
Move on to the usage guide

Use Android / Google TV — Use Remote Help for the staff invitation, code entry, TV permissions, chat and ending the session. No Fire TV Enabler is required. Only share with BM Support staff through your own support ticket or secure order. Do not post your TV code publicly. Anything visible on the TV may be seen by staff: close banking, payment, password and other private screens first. You can decline a request or end a session.
